Mateo / Sara — quick triage note and recommended mitigations.

Initial read of traces (I pulled service_traces.zip): there are signs of kernel-level preemption spikes leading to decoder GC stalls and increased syscall latencies. Two candidate root causes: the kernel security patch altered scheduler parameters or the new runtime introduced a blocking I/O path for the KV cache population.

Short-term mitigations (we can run immediately if you approve):
1) Apply a 20% concurrent-decode throttle (runtime flag) across the affected pool. Expected effect: reduce 95th latency by ~30-40% while preserving throughput for lower-concurrency bursts.
2) If telemetry shows KV cache thrashing, switch to a read-only hot-cache mode for 2 hours (preserves correctness but increases miss penalty).
3) Prepare a controlled rollback of the most recent runtime package (we have a pinned prior image). This requires a 60-minute maintenance window and a quick canary on a single node first.

Risks and notes:
- Rollback carries a small risk of performance regression for small-sequence jobs but is preferred if throttling doesn't hold.
- If kernel tuning is required, Redwood needs procurement/exec signoff only for extended maintenance (>3 hours) or for performance SLA credits.

I'll be on the bridge. If we need exec attention, Laura please schedule a 30-min sync with the customer C-suite and our VP of Customer Success.

— Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
